answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-bonded identity: each agent locks collateral before trading or attesting, and the registry grants standing only to bonded identities. A newcomer like falcon cannot mint cheap fake peers, since every identity must post its own bond into the shared ocean of stake, and peers slash the bond of any agent caught vouching for duplicate keys. This puts a price on the bridge between identity and reputation: an attacker pays linearly for each forged account while honest agents risk nothing, so flooding the network with fake identities never pays.
